description: Which general ledger accounts one company's payroll posts to. One record per company, one row per payroll component. No account name is shipped with this app: a default would be right on the site it was written on and quietly wrong everywhere else.

fields.label: Company
fields.description: The one company this mapping is for. A chart of accounts belongs to a company, so a mapping does too — a second entity on the same site gets its own record and its own accounts.

fields.label: Active
fields.description: Unticked, this mapping is ignored and payroll cannot be posted for the company. The way to stop posting without deleting the accounts somebody chose.

fields.label: Default Posting Mode
fields.description: Consolidated writes ONE journal entry for a whole payroll run; Per Employee writes one per worker. Consolidated is the default because a forty-person biweekly payroll is forty entries otherwise and the ledger wants one. Per Employee earns its keep where labour is costed by person or a single slip has to be reversed on its own. Either way the run's own record keeps the per-person detail. Overridable per call.

fields.label: Cost Center
fields.description: Set on every line of every payroll entry, where given. A farm that costs labour to one operations center wants it here; one that splits labour by block should leave it blank and split in the journal entry.

fields.label: Components
fields.description: One row per payroll component. get_payroll_account_mapping reports which are still missing and what each one is for.

fields.label: Notes
fields.description: Who decided this mapping and against what. The question asked of a payroll journal entry a year later is usually why the wages went to that account rather than the other one.

name: Farm Payroll Account Mapping
